stat.purpose: Header metric numbers. Tight, tabular figures.

body.purpose: The reading base; sans, the narrator voice.

small.purpose: Small body and controls: lede, question text, tabs, metadata, summaries, footer.

label.purpose: Uppercase level names, section headings, captions, buttons, counts, hints.

data.purpose: Database-produced values: SQL, schema fields, result tables, chips, Q-number tag.

meta.purpose: Fine print: column types, FK references, paths, timings, the schema legend.

badge.purpose: PK / FK / UQ role badges; smallest step, bold, mono.

shadows.name: paper-lift
shadows.purpose: The single soft shadow, on cards / tab-bar / table headers so white surfaces don't dissolve into the near-white paper.

motion.name: state-fast
motion.purpose: Default state transition for hover on tabs, buttons, cards, links (color/border/background/transform).

motion.name: target-flash
motion.purpose: One-shot terracotta background flash on the query panel you jumped to, to orient the reader.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion collapses all transitions/animations and disables the hover rise and smooth scroll.

breakpoints.name: none
breakpoints.purpose: No width breakpoints. All responsiveness via flex-wrap + clamp() + min(…,100%). Only media queries are prefers-color-scheme, prefers-reduced-motion, and print.

components.name: Project Tabs
components.description: The primary navigation: one rounded tab-bar surface holding the five project tabs; selected fills terracotta.
components.css: .ds-tabbar { display:inline-flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:.3rem; padding:.3rem; background:var(--card,#fff); border:1px solid var(--line,#e5e1db); border-radius:11px; box-shadow:0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,.05),0 4px 12px rgba(0,0,0,.04); } .ds-tab { display:flex; align-items:center; gap:.45rem; padding:.5rem .75rem; border:0; border-radius:8px; background:transparent; color:var(--mut,#6b6862); font:550 .85rem ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif; cursor:pointer; transition:background .12s,color .12s; } .ds-tab:hover { background:var(--bg,#fbfaf9); color:var(--fg,#1a1917); } .ds-tab.is-selected { background:var(--accent,#b8532a); color:#fff; } .ds-tnum { display:grid; place-items:center; width:1.3rem; height:1.3rem; border-radius:50%; background:var(--line,#e5e1db); color:var(--fg,#1a1917); font-size:.7rem; font-weight:700; } .ds-tab.is-selected .ds-tnum { background:rgba(255,255,255,.25); color:#fff; } .ds-tcount { font-size:.7rem; opacity:.7; font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums; }

components.name: Toolbar Button
components.description: Quiet secondary action (Expand all / Collapse all); hover shifts text + border to terracotta with no fill change.
components.css: .ds-toolbar-btn { font:550 .76rem ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif; padding:.32rem .7rem; cursor:pointer; color:var(--mut,#6b6862); background:var(--card,#fff); border:1px solid var(--line,#e5e1db); border-radius:7px; transition:color .12s,border-color .12s; } .ds-toolbar-btn:hover { color:var(--accent,#b8532a); border-color:var(--accent,#b8532a); } .ds-toolbar-btn:focus-visible { outline:2px solid var(--accent,#b8532a); outline-offset:3px; }

components.name: Question Card
components.description: The workhorse: Q-number, business question, and a footer with row count + timing + a view-SQL affordance. Flat at rest, rises 2px on hover.
components.html:

Which international customers are worth the most, by lifetime value and product variety?

components.css: .ds-card { display:flex; flex-direction:column; background:var(--card,#fff); border:1px solid var(--line,#e5e1db); border-radius:10px; padding:.8rem .9rem .85rem; text-decoration:none; color:inherit; box-shadow:0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,.05),0 4px 12px rgba(0,0,0,.04); transition:transform .12s,border-color .12s; } .ds-card:hover { transform:translateY(-2px); border-color:var(--accent,#b8532a); } .ds-qn { font-size:.7rem; font-weight:700; color:var(--accent,#b8532a); letter-spacing:.06em; } .ds-q { margin:.25rem 0 .6rem; font-size:.89rem; line-height:1.5; flex:1; } .ds-file { display:flex; justify-content:space-between; align-items:baseline; gap:.5rem; font-size:.66rem; color:var(--mut,#6b6862); font-family:ui-monospace,SFMono-Regular,Menlo,monospace; } .ds-go { color:var(--accent,#b8532a); font-weight:600; opacity:.75; } .ds-card:hover .ds-go { opacity:1; }

narrative.overview: The system is an accounts ledger rendered with the warmth of an editorial page. A ledger's job is to reconcile: every value is accounted for, every column lines up, and nothing is fabricated — which is exactly the product's promise (queries written against what the data actually contains, 113/113 verified, caveats named rather than hidden). Monospace carries anything that is data — schema fields, SQL, result rows, paths, timings — so the reader can trust it is the literal record. Proportional sans carries the reading — the business questions, the teaching prose, the labels — so the page stays a document you want to stay inside, not a console you endure. Warmth keeps the rigor from turning clinical: a warm off-white paper ground, a brown-black ink, and a single terracotta accent that reads like a proofreader's red pencil. Surfaces are flat and quiet at rest, separated by hairlines, and lift only when touched. The world rejects the cold high-chrome developer dashboard and the flat generic docs template alike — this is paper-and-pencil precision, not a control panel.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper ground, brown-black ink, a single terracotta accent used sparingly.
Monospace for anything that is data; proportional sans for anything that is reading.
Flat by default; a soft ambient shadow and a 2px rise appear only on interaction.
Hairline borders and generous radii do the separating; color is reserved for meaning.
Fluid and intrinsic — the layout reflows by content weight, with no width breakpoints.

rules.name: The One Pencil Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one brand accent (Terracotta Pencil) and it stays rare — Q-numbers, active state, links, focus. If a screen looks terracotta-heavy, it's wrong; the accent earns attention by scarcity.

rules.name: The Color-Is-Meaning Rule
rules.body: A hue only appears when it encodes something true — a key role, a difficulty level, a syntax token. No color is used to decorate a surface. Neutrals and hairlines do all the structural work.

rules.name: The Record-Is-Mono Rule
rules.body: If a value came out of the database — a column name, a SQL token, a result cell, a row count, a millisecond timing — it is set in monospace. If a human wrote it to teach, it is set in sans. Never blur the two.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat and hairline-bordered at rest. Motion and shadow are earned by interaction (hover, focus, the target flash) — never applied as baseline decoration.

rules.name: The Contained-Scroll Rule
rules.body: Overflow is always solved inside a bordered box (.tblwrap, pre.sql) — the page body itself never scrolls sideways.

dos: Do keep the accent rare — Terracotta Pencil for Q-numbers, active state, links, and focus only (The One Pencil Rule).
Do set every database-produced value (columns, SQL, result cells, counts, timings) in monospace, and every human explanation in sans (The Record-Is-Mono Rule).
Do keep surfaces flat with hairline borders at rest; reserve the Paper Lift shadow and the 2px rise for interaction (The Flat-By-Default Rule).
Do solve overflow inside bordered scroll boxes so the page never scrolls sideways (The Contained-Scroll Rule).
Do let content weight drive density — more words, fewer columns.
Do provide full dark-scheme counterparts for every token; the warm-paper character must survive into dark (warm near-black, not cold charcoal).
donts: Don't spend color on decoration — a hue must encode a key role, a difficulty level, or a syntax token (The Color-Is-Meaning Rule).

Don't rely on hue alone to tell difficulty from schema role: the level colors (green/gold/terracotta/violet) currently reuse the badge hues (FK/PK/accent/UQ), so always pair level color with its dot + uppercase label.
Don't introduce webfonts, gradients, neon-on-charcoal dashboard styling, or heavy drop shadows — they break the paper-and-pencil world.
Don't mute text with opacity (it drops small text under contrast minimums); reach for the Muted Stone token instead.
Don't bake content into markup — the surface is a thin shell rendered from data; keep it that way.
